display.purpose: Stat tile values on Home. The largest numbers in the system. Bold, tabular.

headline.purpose: Card titles. Medium weight Inter, no separate display face.

title.purpose: Nav link labels, button labels, dialog headings.

body.purpose: Default body text. Cap line length at 65 to 75ch for prose.

label.purpose: UPPERCASE tracked label that marks the start of a section. The SectionHeading pattern.

mono.purpose: JetBrains Mono. Reserved for counts, IDs, ratios, durations, keyboard shortcuts.

shadows.name: slot-hover
shadows.purpose: Box slot interactive feedback. Hover only. Equivalent to Tailwind shadow-md.

shadows.name: pip
shadows.purpose: Lifts shiny and registration pips off the sprite background. Equivalent to shadow-sm.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, alert dialogs, sheets. Available as the shadow-overlay utility (defined in globals.css).

motion.name: transition-normal
motion.purpose: State changes, theme transitions, drop indicators.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: System default. Set via --default-transition-timing-function so every transition-* utility without an explicit easing eases out exponentially. Also available as the ease-out-quart utility class.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Reserved for explicit layout-transform overrides (sidebar collapse, padding shifts). Never the default; opt in by setting ease-in-out on the element.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The confirmation button. Used for primary CTAs (Save, Confirm, Create). Never colored with Signal Red.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; gap: 6px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; background: #252525; color: #ffffff; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1), transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1); outline: none; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1a1a1a; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { border-color: #e63946; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(230 57 70 / 0.5); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The everyday button. Auto-fill, Edit, secondary CTAs. Quiet at rest.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; gap: 6px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; background: #f8f9fa; color: #171717; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1), border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1); outline: none; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #f1f5f9; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { border-color: #e63946; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(230 57 70 / 0.5); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Transparent until hover. Icon-only actions in headers and toolbars.

components.name: Input
components.description: Text input with Signal Red focus glow. The primary focus treatment across the system.

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat surface with a hairline ring instead of a border or shadow. The default container.

components.name: Stat Tile
components.description: Compact KPI block for the Home page. Display-size number, mono sub, muted label. Not the hero-metric template: every value is the same size; rhythm comes from the grid, not from oversized digits.

components.name: Type Chip
components.description: Pokémon type chip. Type color carries identity, glyph and text carry accessibility. Color is never the sole signal.
components.css: .ds-chip-type { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; height: 20px; padding: 0 8px 0 4px; border-radius: 26px; color: #ffffff; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip-glyph { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 999px; background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.25); font-size: 0.625rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-chip-type--fire { background: #F08030; }

components.name: Box Slot (Registered)
components.description: Signature component. A 6x5 grid of these makes up every box. Registered state: sprite at 100%, green check pip in top-right.
components.html: 🌱
components.css: .ds-slot { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 72px; height: 72px; border-radius: 10px; background: #ffffff; cursor: pointer; outline: none; transition: box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1), transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1); } .ds-slot:hover { box-shadow: 0 4px 8px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.10), 0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.06); } .ds-slot:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #252525; } .ds-slot-sprite { font-size: 36px; line-height: 1; transition: transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1); } .ds-slot:hover .ds-slot-sprite { transform: scale(1.1); } .ds-slot-check { position: absolute; top: 2px; right: 2px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 999px; background: #16a34a; color: #ffffff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); }

narrative.overview: The interface is the binder; the user's Pokémon are the content. Every surface is neutral and quiet so that sprites, registration checks, shiny pips, and type chips carry every meaningful color on the screen. The only saturated tone in the chrome is Signal Red, used sparingly to mark exactly one thing at a time: which navigation item is active, which slot is selected, where the focus ring sits. Everything else is a tinted neutral. The system honors Pokémon Home's 6x5 grid as a literal structural element, then dresses it down. No pixel fonts, no glossy badge buttons, no red-yellow gradients, no celebratory motion. The reward for using this tool is the user's own sense of order, not the tool congratulating them. Density is moderate and considered: the home page leads with one progress ring, then a tight 3 to 4 column grid of stat tiles, then quiet section strips. The visual language sits in the same neighborhood as Linear, Things 3, and Raycast; it explicitly rejects every Pokémon fan dashboard since 2008.
keyCharacteristics: One saturated brand color (Signal Red), used as a state marker on <=5% of any screen.
Tinted-neutral surface ramp with a hairline ring (ring-1 ring-foreground/10) instead of borders or shadows on cards.
Inter for everything, JetBrains Mono reserved for IDs, counts, and small metadata.
Spacing rhythm in 4/8/12/16/24px steps; uppercase tracked-wide labels mark section starts.
Type colors live exclusively inside data (chips, stat grids). They never leak into the chrome.

rules.name: The Signal Red Rule
rules.body: Signal Red marks the answer to 'where am I?' or 'what did I just pick?' on a given screen. If a second element is competing for that answer, one of them is wrong. Never use Signal Red for hover states, for non-selection highlights, for decorative borders, for chart series, or for type/generation chips.

rules.name: The Type-Color Containment Rule
rules.body: Pokémon type colors live inside data, never around it. A type chip can be #F08030. A card containing a Fire-type Pokémon cannot be #F08030. Backgrounds, borders, headers, and dividers never inherit type color.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutral Direction
rules.body: Every neutral carries chroma. In light mode, push hue 25 (warm, toward Signal Red) at chroma 0.005 to 0.02. In dark mode, the surface family (Surface, Muted, Border) keeps hue 270 (cool, toward #1a1a2e) for depth; content surfaces (Card, Popover, Foreground, Primary) tint warm so they read as content against the cool chrome. No pure #000, no pure #fff, ever.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Numbers Rule
rules.body: Anything that's a count, an ID, a ratio, or a duration uses JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums. Anything that's a name, a label, or prose uses Inter. The rule is mechanical; there are no exceptions.

rules.name: The Tracked-Label Rule
rules.body: Section starts are signaled by an uppercase, tracked, muted-foreground label, never by an oversized heading. The Home page is the reference: SectionHeading is the smallest type on the page, not the largest.

rules.name: The No-Hero-Type Rule
rules.body: No clamp(2rem, 7vw, 5rem) hero displays. The largest type in the product is the 24px stat value. Drama comes from rhythm, not from scale.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If a card has a shadow with no interaction, it's wrong; replace the shadow with a ring-1 ring-foreground/10.

rules.name: The Ring-Over-Border Rule
rules.body: For card-like containers, prefer ring-1 over border so the stroke doesn't shift the box model. Borders are reserved for inputs, navigation rails, and dividers; rings for cards and overlays.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow on a stat tile, a section header, a chip, or a sidebar item is always wrong. Shadows are feedback. If something doesn't respond to the cursor or keyboard, it doesn't get a shadow.

dos: Do use Signal Red (#e63946) as a state marker only: active nav, selected slot, focus ring, primary CTA never (use Neutral Primary #252525 for primary CTAs).
Do use ring-1 ring-foreground/10 for card-like containers; reserve border for inputs, nav rails, and dividers.
Do use JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums for every count, ID, ratio, and duration. Use Inter for everything else.
Do lead a section with text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-muted-foreground (the SectionHeading pattern). The Home page is the canonical reference.

Do pair every color signal with a glyph, abbreviation, or text. Type chips always carry the type name; registered slots always carry the green check; shiny slots always carry the sparkle. Color is never the sole signal.

Do lean on the default easing. --ease-out-quart (cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1)) is set as --default-transition-timing-function, so every transition-* utility without an explicit easing eases out exponentially. Use ease-out-quart when an explicit easing class is needed. Reserve ease-in-out for explicit layout-transform overrides only.
Do keep transition durations on the existing tokens: --transition-fast 150ms, --transition-normal 200ms, --transition-slow 300ms.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: every transition currently uses motion-reduce:transition-none, and new ones must too.
Do use the existing radius scale (6/10/12/14/26 px) rather than inventing new values.
Do keep the type-color palette (src/lib/type-colors.ts) inside Pokémon data: type chips, the stats type grid, search result rows. Nowhere else.
donts: Don't use pixel fonts, Game Boy bezels, glossy 3D pokéballs, red/yellow gradient backgrounds, pokéball-shaped buttons, sparkle effects in chrome, or 'Gotta catch 'em all' copy. The fan-site lane is off-limits.
Don't ship the generic SaaS look: off-white plus single blue accent, identical icon-and-heading card grids, hero-metric blocks, gradient pill buttons.
Don't ship loud gamified RPG dashboards: animated stat bars, level-up flourishes, neon glows, badge spam, particle effects, achievement toasts, XP rings, combo celebrations.
Don't ship the bento-grid AI app look: rounded-2xl cards in a 12-column bento, glass blurs, gradient mesh backgrounds, oversized hero typography that says nothing.
Don't use Signal Red (#e63946) for hover states, dividers, chart series, decorative borders, or any non-selection highlight.
Don't use any of the 18 Pokémon type colors outside of type chips, the stats type grid, or search result rows.
Don't add border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. Gradient text is absolutely banned.
Don't use blurs or glass cards as a default treatment.
Don't reach for a modal first. Use inline editing wherever possible.
Don't ship pure #ffffff or pure #000000 in new tokens. Every neutral carries chroma 0.005 to 0.02 at hue 25 (light, content surfaces in dark) or hue 270 (dark surface family).
Don't add drop shadows to surfaces at rest. If you want depth, use the ring; if you want emphasis, use weight or spacing.
Don't invent a new font, weight, or size scale outside the existing hierarchy. Inter + JetBrains Mono is the entire system.
Don't localize 'PokeBox' or product strings into emoji or icon-only forms. pt-BR is the default locale and gets first-class strings.
Don't ship a 'completion celebration' animation. The user's count going up is the reward. No confetti, no toast, no sound.
